hook: SCP-748 starts as a site survey of a rusted complex hidden beneath an old Lowell textile mill, then widens into a biography of the mill's owner and a bundle of letters and diaries from the people who worked there. Read the floors in order, because each one is labeled like a department of a business. Further down there is something that can still talk, and the document you are reading does not stay the same document all the way through. Expect forced labor, beatings and surgical mutilation described plainly.
whyItMatters:
This is industrial horror built from labor history: a factory owner praised as a self-made philanthropist, a bombed mill blamed on anarchists, and a hidden plant where workers are used up and fed back into the machinery. The posters with cheerful slogans and the owner's talk of the invisible hand of the market make the critique of unchecked industry hard to miss.

It also opens a much larger frame than one building. A shadowy backer called the Investor is logged as a person of interest, and the text hints that this plant was only one of many.
thingsToNotice:
The crate inventory is a deliberately absurd catalogue of goods nobody should sell: radioactive rocking horses that scream when watched, fur coats that never stop burning, and cigarettes that turn a smoker into a basking shark before he explodes. After that the documents run on two tracks, with Metzger's diary climbing from a signed deal to calling himself God of the factory and finally to fearing he is obsolete, while the workers slide from Brianna's hopeful letter (which notes his wife and sons have stopped visiting) to faceless overseers, vanishing coworkers and the scraping Harvestmen at night.

The autopsy note that his brain was never found pays off on the fourth floor, where a living brain wired into a 275-ton machine claims to be Metzger and dismisses the 200 lobotomized brains around it as spare memory. Once staff begin vanishing whenever they step out of sight, the file is overwritten by an O5 version dated the last day of 1999: Site-68's own personnel have become skinless, faceless harvesters with cages on their backs, and the factory's goods turn up in ordinary shops where the money paid for them simply disappears. The recovered audio ends with the brain calling up Liverpool and Tokyo and announcing that business is open again.
